summary_of_change:
Ferrari's operational execution across recent quarters demonstrates exceptional pricing power, though deliberate volume control is evident. In Q2 2026, net revenues reached €1,938M ($2,131.8M), representing an annualized run-rate of $8,527.2M. Gross margin held firm at 48.5%, while EBIT margin expanded to 31.2% (€605M). Quarterly shipments totaled 3,366 units (annualizing to ~13,464 units), reflecting planned model changeovers as legacy lines like the SF90 XX and Roma Spider phase out to make way for the 12Cilindri, 849 Testarossa, and Amalfi ramps.

Monetization yield remains highly lucrative. Average Selling Price (ASP) reached ~€487k per unit in Q2 2026, driven by a 16% volume contribution from Special Series models and limited hypercars like the F80. Personalization sales continue to exceed 20% of vehicle and spare parts revenue. Following strong H1 performance, management raised full-year 2026 guidance, targeting ~€7.6B in net revenue, ≥€2.97B in adjusted EBITDA, and ≥€1.55B in Industrial Free Cash Flow, with the order book fully sold out through the entirety of 2027.

Capital allocation remains balanced between internal growth projects and shareholder returns. In H1 2026, Ferrari distributed €599 million in cash dividends and repurchased €254.5 million of common stock under its ongoing buyback program. Continued cancellation of treasury shares reduces the diluted share count to 176.0M shares, concentrating cash flows per share despite ongoing CapEx deployment into electrification and battery assembly at the Maranello e-building.

market_pricing_in:
At today's market price of $419.92 (53.1x P/OE and 54.4x EV/OE), Mr. Market is pricing Ferrari N.V. not as an automotive manufacturer, but as a bulletproof luxury monopoly comparable to Hermès. The market embeds complete confidence that Ferrari can perpetually expand average selling prices (ASPs), scale high-margin personalization options above 20% of revenue, and seamlessly pass cost inflation to its Ultra-High-Net-Worth buyer base. Wall Street's prevailing multiple assumes that the pre-sold order backlog stretching through calendar year 2027 provides absolute immunity against macroeconomic cycles.

However, sell-side bear notes (including downgrades and cautious commentary from Morgan Stanley and Bernstein) highlight growing operational vulnerabilities. Delivery volumes contracted in major markets like North America during Q2 2026, confirming that Ferrari is reaching its self-imposed annual volume cap of ~14,000 units. Furthermore, the unveiling of the all-electric Ferrari Luce at €550,000 generated mixed dealer feedback, introducing platform transition risks. Fixed capitalized R&D amortization from the Maranello e-building is beginning to hit the income statement, while H2 2026 USD/EUR foreign exchange exposure remains under-hedged, creating unpriced earnings drag.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: Normalized Owner Earnings stand at $7.90/share ($1,391.0M total) with net balance sheet cash/debt of $-10.48/share ($-1,844M net debt).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: If a global economic contraction impacts ultra-wealthy consumers, high-margin personalization add-ons (carbon fiber, bespoke leathers, historical paint formulas) could compress from >20% down to 12% of vehicle sales. Concurrently, unhedged foreign exchange volatility creates margin drag, while fixed D&A burdens (>€700M/year) from the e-building and EV infrastructure cannot be scaled back.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Annual shipments contract from 13,464 units down to 12,200 units as model changeovers lag and discretionary buyers delay order placements. Reduced personalization take-rates compress revenue yield per unit, driving run-rate revenue down from $8,527.2M to $6,950M.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Sticky fixed cash expenses (F1 racing operations, centralized Maranello plant overhead, capitalized R&D amortization) compress gross margins to 43.0%. Normalized total Owner Earnings degrade sharply to $4.50/share ($792M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Applying a trough 10.0x P/OE multiple to degraded Owner Earnings of $4.50/share yields $45.00/share equity value, plus ending net debt of $-10.48/share, establishing a Downside Risk Valuation Floor of $34.52/share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: Current annualized volume run-rate is 13,464 vehicle shipments (3,366 units in Q2 2026) generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $8,527.2M, representing an effective monetization yield of ~$633.3k gross revenue per unit across cars, personalizations, sponsorships, and spare parts.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Enforcing strict brand scarcity and capped annual factory output, volume shipments expand modestly to 13,700 units in Year 1, 13,950 units in Year 2, and 14,200 units in Year 3 (~1.8% annual volume CAGR).

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue: Assuming total unit monetization yield expands to ~$700k per unit—driven by Daytona SP3 and F80 hypercar deliveries, higher bespoke option uptake, and early deliveries of the Luce EV—Year 3 Revenue reaches 14,200 units × $700k = $9,940.0M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Subtracting projected cash COGS and operating expenses of $6,450.0M, maintenance CapEx of $790.0M, and stock-based compensation of $50.0M yields Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $1,850.0M (18.6% Owner Cash Margin, or $10.51/share on 176.0M diluted shares).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash is $-1,844.0M ($-10.48/sh). Because Starting Net Cash is negative, exactly $0.00 is allocated to share buybacks. Cumulative 3Y Free Cash Flow generated of $4,800.0M minus cumulative growth CapEx of $2,400.0M results in net balance sheet cash generation of +$2,400.0M, bringing Ending Year 3 Net Cash to +$556.0M (+$3.16/share).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate (g₃) is 10.1% YoY ($9.55/sh in Year 2 to $10.51/sh in Year 3), placing RACE in the Steady Compounding tier (8%–15% growth) of the Wide Moat Matrix. Applying the disciplined 20.0x P/OE exit multiple yields an equity capitalized value of $210.20/share ($10.51 × 20.0x). Adding ending net cash of +$3.16/share delivers an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $213.36/share. From today's market price of $419.92, this indicates an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of -20.2% per annum due to severe multiple compression.

What the Market is Pricing In

At today's market price of $419.92 (53.1x P/OE and 54.4x EV/OE), Mr. Market is pricing Ferrari N.V. not as an automotive manufacturer, but as a bulletproof luxury monopoly comparable to Hermès. The market embeds complete confidence that Ferrari can perpetually expand average selling prices (ASPs), scale high-margin personalization options above 20% of revenue, and seamlessly pass cost inflation to its Ultra-High-Net-Worth buyer base. However, sell-side bear notes (including downgrades and cautious commentary from Morgan Stanley and Bernstein) highlight growing operational vulnerabilities. Delivery volumes contracted in major markets like North America during Q2 2026, confirming that Ferrari is reaching its self-imposed annual volume cap of ~14,000 units. Furthermore, the unveiling of the all-electric Ferrari Luce at €550,000 generated mixed dealer feedback, introducing platform transition risks. Fixed capitalized R&D amortization from the Maranello e-building is beginning to hit the income statement, while H2 2026 USD/EUR foreign exchange exposure remains under-hedged, creating unpriced earnings drag.

Concurrently, unhedged foreign exchange volatility creates margin drag, while fixed D&A burdens (>€700M/year) from the e-building and EV infrastructure cannot be scaled back.

Capital allocation remains balanced between internal growth projects and shareholder returns. Continued cancellation of treasury shares reduces the diluted share count to 176.0M shares, concentrating cash flows per share despite ongoing CapEx deployment into electrification and battery assembly at the Maranello e-building.
